title: Agile Space Industries Celebrates Durango Headquarters Expansion with Ribbon Cutting
summary: Agile Space Industries celebrated the completion of a 20,500-square-foot expansion of its Durango headquarters with a ribbon-cutting ceremony on August 26, 2026. The event highlighted the company's growth in its facilities.

title: Commercial Space Federation (CSF) Welcomes Two New Associate Members
summary: The Commercial Space Federation (CSF) announced the addition of two new associate members, Outlier and Rendezvous Robotics, which specialize in reusable satellite platforms and adaptable technologies. This move expands the CSF's network in the commercial space sector.

title: Speed to Field Starts Below the Prime
summary: The article discusses the defense industrial base from various perspectives, including a warfighter's viewpoint and insights from leading a company in the sector. It emphasizes the importance of speed in fielding capabilities.

summary: SpaceNews interviews Jeff Janicik, founder and chairman of Innoflight, about space networking electronics, Golden Dome, Artemis, and collaboration with the Space Development Agency.

title: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth Partner to Connect Space and Soil
summary: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth have partnered to integrate satellite data with ground-based environmental observations for nature-based projects. This collaboration aims to enhance the accuracy and utility of environmental monitoring.

title: RTX’s Blue Canyon Technologies introduces new spacecraft mission enabler
summary: Blue Canyon Technologies, a subsidiary of RTX, has introduced a new spacecraft subsystem aimed at enhancing mission capabilities for small satellites. This innovation is part of RTX's ongoing efforts to advance space technology.

summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a local spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg unveiled NewTEN, a two-axis steerable compact antenna designed to enhance communications for small spacecraft. The product was introduced at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

title: Astronomers discover mysterious 10-sided cloud structure at Saturn's south pole
summary: Astronomers discovered a mysterious 10-sided cloud structure around Saturn's south pole. The unusual pattern was identified in a new study.

title: China's private, reusable Pallas-1 rocket aces debut launch (video)
summary: China's private company Galactic Energy successfully launched its reusable Pallas-1 rocket into orbit on August 31, marking a significant milestone for the country's commercial space sector. The rocket's first stage did not perform a landing attempt during this debut mission.

title: This was always the way: 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' is finally on Disney+
summary: The 'Star Wars' spin-off movie 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' is now available on Disney+. Despite a weak box office performance, it may succeed as a streaming hit.

title: 2 spacecraft headed to Mercury are about to begin their long-awaited arrival for Europe and Japan — watch it live on Sept. 3
summary: The BepiColombo mission, a joint effort by Europe and Japan, is set to begin its arrival phase at Mercury on September 3. The event can be watched live.

summary: NASA has awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract to develop the next Mars telecommunications orbiter. This marks a significant milestone for Blue Origin in interplanetary missions.

summary: The creative director of 'Alien Isolation 2' discusses the sequel's increased scare factor and returning to the franchise after a decade. The game aims to evoke feelings of exposure, vulnerability, and isolation.

title: Supermassive black holes 'too big' for the early universe may not be so massive after all
summary: New research suggests that supermassive black holes detected by the James Webb Space Telescope may not be as massive as previously thought. These findings challenge earlier assumptions about the size of black holes in the early universe.

title: Falcon Heavy brings the heat | Space photo of the day for Sept. 2, 2026
summary: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket launched NASA's Roman Space Telescope on Aug. 30, 2026, captured in a dramatic launch photo. The event highlights SpaceX's continued dominance in heavy-lift launches.

title: On this day in space! Sept. 2, 2016: Rosetta spacecraft finds long-lost Philae lander on Comet 67P after 2-year search
summary: The European Space Agency located its lost Philae lander on Comet 67P after a two-year search. This discovery was significant for the mission's data collection and analysis.

title: Scientists may have detected the 1st direct evidence of dark matter
summary: Scientists may have detected the first direct evidence of dark matter using the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment. This discovery involves a rare interaction between a WIMP particle and ordinary matter.

title: Rocket Lab’s Hungry Hippo completes testing
summary: Rocket Lab has completed testing of its Hungry Hippo payload fairing for the upcoming Neutron rocket. The Neutron vehicle is scheduled for a launch later this year.

title: Launch Site and Facility Progress ahead of East Coast Starship debut
summary: SpaceX is preparing for the upcoming Starship Flight 14 launch from Florida, with progress being made at the launch site and facilities. The East Coast debut of Starship is anticipated in the coming weeks.

summary: Six international space missions are scheduled for launch this week from various global launch sites. The post provides a preview of these upcoming launches.

summary: NASA and its contractors are accelerating work on the Space Launch System (SLS) with four vehicles currently in production ahead of the Artemis III mission planned for next year. The progress marks a significant step toward the agency's lunar exploration goals.

title: NASA, SpaceX successfully launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida
summary: NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. This mission marks a significant step in space observatory development.

summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has signed the first contracts under its European Launcher Challenge, marking a significant step in fostering European launch capabilities. This initiative aims to support innovative launch providers within Europe.

title: Soyuz MS-28 departs the ISS, three spacewalks install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae
summary: Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft departed from the International Space Station. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae.

title: Starbase, Louisiana: The Largest Private Spaceport in the World
summary: SpaceX has announced plans to develop Starbase, Louisiana, which will be the largest private spaceport in the world. The facility aims to support future space missions and launch activities.

summary: Starbase's production capacity is increasing due to heightened activity at the site. This expansion is aimed at supporting future space missions and operations.

summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch NASA's Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites. Five orbital launches are planned this week from China, the U.S., and French Guiana.

summary: The news source is a B2B website focused on the technology, engineering, and construction sectors, covering business-related updates in these industries.

summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements over the past five decades.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona during this event.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event is part of the mission's testing and observation phase.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than during natural eclipses, which are brief and rare.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: ESA is inviting European researchers and companies to run software aboard the Hera mission in deep space. This offers a unique opportunity to test innovations millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, effectively playing 'hide and seek' with Earth's view. The mission aims to achieve unprecedented precision in satellite alignment for solar observations.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: York Space Systems Unveils New VLEO Sat Platform
summary: York Space Systems has introduced a new Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellite platform, aiming to outpace competitors by prioritizing speed to market over lower altitudes.

summary: Astroscale Japan has chosen Germany's Isar Aerospace to launch its ADRAS-J2 mission, which aims to capture and remove a large piece of orbital debris. This collaboration highlights advancements in space debris mitigation technology.

title: Trump Orders Study To Establish US Space Academy
summary: Former President Trump has ordered a study to potentially establish a new US Space Academy, which could introduce another service academy to the existing military academies. This move could spark comparisons to college football rivalries among the service academies.

summary: Helogen is planning two in-orbit manufacturing missions in October, marking the first flights of its HEL-IOS platform. The company has previously flown subsystems but this will be the first time the entire platform is tested in space.

title: Fermi Explorer Wants to Reach Another Star for $15M
summary: The Starcloud cofounders announced the Fermi Explorer mission, aiming to launch humanity's first mission to Alpha Centauri by 2029 with a $15M budget.

summary: Diffraqtion secured additional funding for its quantum camera technology through a pre-seed round led by Lockheed Martin Ventures and Sumitomo Corporation’s Presidio Ventures, bringing its total funding to over $10 million.

summary: Boeing has delivered the final three satellites for SES's O3b mPOWER constellation, which are scheduled for launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 mission later this month.

summary: Telesat is exploring space-to-ground optical communications in a new collaboration with Cailabs. The agreement aims to integrate optical connectivity solutions for potential adoption.

summary: Intuitive Machines has secured a two-satellite order for an unnamed commercial customer using its IM 300 platform, which has previously supported Space Development Agency missions.

summary: Via Satellite celebrates its 40-year history of covering the space and satellite industry, sharing memories from its first edition in 1986 to the present.

title: Space Defense in 2040: A Networked, Weaponized, and Contested Frontier
summary: Autonomous systems, sensors, and AI-driven targeting are expected to revolutionize space defense by 2040, creating a contested and weaponized orbital domain. The article highlights the shift toward networked and AI-optimized warfighting capabilities in space.
